subject: Interactive pivot for high-cost token sequences across multi-model routes
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interactive pivot for high-cost token sequences across multi-model routes

Hey team —

Quick ask from a recent Acme postmortem: they want an investigator UI that lets them pivot from a route to the top-k high-cost token sequences (by USD/token), and then filter that view across model variants and time windows so they can correlate cost spikes with model rollouts and prompt changes.

Why this matters: their finance and SRE teams repeatedly hit bursts where a small set of query prefixes cause outsized token spend across several routes. Today they can pull BigQuery exports but it takes > 24h and manual joins. If we give them a lightweight interactive pivot in Console -> Route Diagnostics, they can:
- identify the top 50 token sequences contributing to cost in an interval
- group by model variant (gpt-x-quant, gpt-x-fp16, llm-lite)
- see tail latency per sequence and per-minute cost impact
- export a CSV or open a sample trace in Trace Playback

Proposed MVP: a read-only explorer panel under Route Diagnostics. Minimal backend: precompute sequence aggregates once per 5m window and store an indexed table. UI: pivot table + sparklines + a ‘Open traces’ button. Attach a rough wireframe and a sample CSV from Acme.

Attachments: prototype-pivot-wireframe.png, sample-high-cost-sequences.csv

Ask: can infra/observability estimate (a) storage/ingest cost for 5m aggregation for top-100 sequences per route, (b) query cost for the explorer, and (c) a safe default retention? Also need PM/UX alignment on filters and export columns.

Rishi
Head of Product Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interactive pivot for high-cost token sequences across multi-model routes

Thanks Rishi — good, concrete ask. A few clarifying questions before I loop infra: 

1) Scope: do we want this explorer to be per-tenant only (Acme wants tenant-scoped first) or per-route globally? My preference is tenant-scoped with a route selector so we avoid cross-tenant aggregation complexity for MVP.

2) Time windows: common use cases are last 1h / 6h / 24h / 7d. Is 5m rollup sufficient for all? If a customer wants sub-1m resolution we should fall back to raw traces with a warning.

3) Exports: CSV is a must-have; would we also provide a pre-built Drive link to sample traces (trace ids) or a Trace Playback button?

Kimberly/Laura — can you weigh in on alerting implications? If customers can see top-k sequences, do we want an accompanying ‘create cost alert’ flow (maybe later) or guardrails to prevent bulk exports causing burst queries?

If infra can provide rough numbers by EOD I’ll add this to next week’s observability prioritization doc.

—Marissa
Product Manager, Console
From: Beth Hart <beth.hart@acme-analytics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: acme-sre@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 12:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interactive pivot for high-cost token sequences across multi-model routes

Appreciate the fast follow. Confirming Acme wants tenant-scoped first. Our SREs would use the pivot to map expensive queries back to release windows — we run model variant A/B rollouts weekly.

Notes from our side:
- Top sequences we care about often include long conversation prefixes with many system messages; sample file attached for context (we exported a previous run).
- A Drive link to sample traces is preferred for quick handoffs to our SRE on-call.
- Retention: 30 days would be fine for exploration, but our billing team wants the aggregate numbers persisted for 90 days.

We opened a ticket on our side (ACME-TKT-778) and pasted a small sample CSV for you.

Beth Hart
Engineering Manager, Platform Reliability
Acme Analytics
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Apr 2028 15:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interactive pivot for high-cost token sequences across multi-model routes

Looping infra/observability offline, but quick takes:

- Tenant-scoped first makes sense. Avoids cross-tenant join complexity.
- 5m rollup + ability to open raw traces for a selected sequence is a good tradeoff.
- For safeguards: limit CSV exports to 10k rows by default and surface a cost estimate prior to export; add a circuit-breaker for simultaneous heavy pivots.
- Estimated engineering effort for an MVP (backend + UI + trace link): 4-6 sprints across two teams if we build a new aggregation pipeline. If we can reuse existing summary tables (OBS_SUMMARY_5M), effort drops to 2-3 sprints.
- Storage delta for top-100 per-route at 5m windows: roughly 120 GiB/month for us-west with current customer scale (ballpark). Query cost depends on sample retention; I’ll follow up with a short cost estimate and a Jira (OBS-1248) to track.

I’ll raise this in today’s observability sync and add the wireframe to the ticket.

Kimberly
Director, Observability Engineering
Redwood Inference
